answer: An agent market requires every identity to lock collateral for 30 days before it can accept jobs; its payment bridge checks that bond on a public ledger, which serves as a shared trust beacon. A sable avatar or fresh name cannot reuse another account’s collateral. Creating 1,000 eligible identities therefore requires 1,000 separate bonds, tying up the attacker’s capital for the full period. This prices identity multiplication rather than pretending to prove uniqueness.
